text.p: Continental Airlines said it was considering launching an airport-to-door cargo service from Europe to the U.S.
Andreas Gutberlet, newly-appointed cargo sales manager Germany, told Reuters he favoured such a product as an addition to the airline's existing airport-to-airport services.
"As a belly carrier we have a lot of consolidated freight. I am thinking about a more active product for small shipments on new routes," he said.
"We are looking to see whether we can offer airport-to-door which could be either from Germany or from the UK."
A potential problem for such a service, however, was lack of information technology links and forwarder experience in such fields, Gutbertlet added.
"We will certainly not invest without looking at the market very closely and making sure the idea is right," he said.

About 40-50 percent of Continental's ex-Germany freight was destined for New York, with most heavy weight for the east coast, medium-weight freight often heading to Atlanta or the Mid West and smaller freight transhipped to the west coast.
Continental aimed to improve its contacts with German air cargo shippers and to be more aware of their needs but not at the cost of freight forwarders, Gutberlet said.

"We have contacts with air cargo shippers but only in cooperation with freight forwarders. We will not have any direct contacts with shippers. It makes no sense to exclude agents who do all the work in the market," he stressed.
The airline wanted to maintain a wide base of forwarder clients and sought to work with large and small forwarders alike, he added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
